known_pitfall_claim: The proof claims that e^{((2k+1)/2)(2iπ/n)}(e^{-iπ/n}-e^{iπ/n}) equals e^{((2k+1)/2)(2iπ/n)}·2i sin(π/n), with a positive sign.
pitfall_counterexample: Use complex numbers with k=0 and n=2. Then A=((2k+1)/2)(2iπ/n)=iπ/2, exp(A)=i, sin(π/n)=1, exp(-iπ/n)=-i, and exp(iπ/n)=i. Thus the original expression is i·((-i)-i)=i·(-2i)=2, while the claimed positive-sign expression is i·2i·1=-2.
